title: Zechariah Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Zechariah chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Zechariah Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Zechariah Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Zechariah 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The burden of the word of the LORD
Tyrus did build herself a strong hold
A bastard shall dwell in Ashdod
questions.correctAnswer: The burden of the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: The phrase 'The burden of the word of the LORD' appears first in Zechariah 9:1.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned as bordering Hamath?
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus
questions.explanation: Tyrus is mentioned as bordering Hamath in Zechariah 9:2.

questions.question: What did Tyrus heap up according to Zechariah 9?
options: Gold as the mire of the streets
questions.correctAnswer: Silver as the dust
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:3 states that Tyrus heaped up 'silver as the dust'.

questions.question: What will the Lord do to Tyrus?
questions.correctAnswer: Cast her out
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:4 states that 'the Lord will cast her out'.

questions.question: Which city shall see it and fear according to Zechariah 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Ashkelon
questions.explanation: Ashkelon is mentioned as seeing it and fearing in Zechariah 9:5.

questions.question: What shall happen to the king of Gaza?
questions.correctAnswer: He shall perish
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:5 states that 'the king shall perish from Gaza'.

questions.question: What shall happen to Ashkelon according to Zechariah 9?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be inhabited
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:5 indicates that 'Ashkelon shall not be inhabited'.

questions.question: Who will dwell in Ashdod?
questions.correctAnswer: A bastard
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:6 states that 'a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod'.

questions.question: What will happen to the pride of the Philistines?
questions.correctAnswer: It will be cut off
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:6 states 'I will cut off the pride of the Philistines'.

questions.question: What is the land mentioned in Zechariah 9:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Hadrach
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:1 mentions 'the land of Hadrach'.

questions.question: What is said to be very wise in Zechariah 9?
questions.correctAnswer: Zidon
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:2 states that 'Zidon, though it be very wise'.

questions.question: True or False: Damascus is mentioned in Zechariah 9:1.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Damascus is indeed mentioned in Zechariah 9:1.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will smite her power in the land.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Lord will smite her power in the sea as stated in Zechariah 9:4.

questions.question: True or False: Ashdod will be a prosperous city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not say Ashdod will be prosperous; it states a bastard shall dwell there in Zechariah 9:6.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Ashkelon shall reign forever.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text states the king shall perish from Gaza, not that Ashkelon shall have a reigning king in Zechariah 9:5.

medium.title: Zechariah Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Zechariah Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 9:9, how does the King come to Jerusalem?
options: Riding upon an ass and upon a colt the foal of an ass
On foot with a mighty army
questions.correctAnswer: Riding upon an ass and upon a colt the foal of an ass
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 describes the King as coming lowly, riding upon an ass and upon a colt the foal of an ass.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 9:12 promise will happen if prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold as commanded in verse 11?
options: God will render double unto them
They will be sent back to the pit
questions.correctAnswer: God will render double unto them
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:12 promises that if prisoners of hope turn to the stronghold (verse 11), God will render double unto them.

questions.question: What will be cut off from Ephraim according to Zechariah 9:10?
questions.correctAnswer: The chariot
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:10 states that the chariot will be cut off from Ephraim.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 9:7 relate to Zechariah 9:8 in terms of God's protection?
options: God removes abominations and encamps around His house to protect it from armies
God allows oppressors to pass and weakens the house
God removes rulers and abandons the house
God increases the army and destroys the house
questions.correctAnswer: God removes abominations and encamps around His house to protect it from armies
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:7 talks about removing abominations and appointing governors, while 9:8 describes God encamping around His house to protect it from armies and oppressors.

questions.question: How does the promise of peace in Zechariah 9:10 affect the dominion of the King?
options: His dominion will extend from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth
His dominion will be limited to Jerusalem only
His dominion will be challenged by many wars
His dominion will be over just Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: His dominion will extend from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:10 states that the King shall speak peace to the heathen and his dominion will be from sea to sea and to the ends of the earth.

questions.question: What practical lesson can believers learn from God removing 'his blood out of his mouth' in Zechariah 9:7?
options: God cleanses corrupt speech and evil influence
God allows evil to remain unchecked
God ignores the sins of leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God cleanses corrupt speech and evil influence
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:7 metaphorically describes removing blood and abominations from the mouth and teeth, symbolizing God cleansing corrupt speech and evil influence.

questions.question: What assurance does Zechariah 9:8 give regarding oppressors and God's awareness?
options: No oppressor shall pass through them any more because God has seen with His eyes
Oppressors will continue to roam freely
questions.correctAnswer: No oppressor shall pass through them any more because God has seen with His eyes
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:8 assures that God encamps around His house and no oppressor shall pass because He has seen with His eyes.

questions.question: How can the promise in Zechariah 9:11 encourage believers today who feel trapped or imprisoned?
options: God sends forth prisoners out of the pit by the blood of the covenant
Believers are left to free themselves
questions.correctAnswer: God sends forth prisoners out of the pit by the blood of the covenant
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:11 offers hope by declaring that God sends forth prisoners out of the pit by the blood of the covenant.

questions.question: What does the humility of the King in Zechariah 9:9 teach about leadership?
options: True leadership is marked by humility and justice
Leadership requires grand displays of power
questions.correctAnswer: True leadership is marked by humility and justice
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 describes the King as just and lowly, riding an ass rather than a horse or chariot, teaching humility in leadership.

questions.question: What impact does the cutting off of the battle bow in Zechariah 9:10 have on the nations?
options: Peace will be spoken unto the heathen
The bow remains a symbol of power
questions.correctAnswer: Peace will be spoken unto the heathen
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:10 says the battle bow will be cut off and the King will speak peace to the heathen, indicating a cessation of war.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 9:12 encourage believers facing trials or imprisonment?
options: They are called prisoners of hope and promised double restoration
They are told to give up hope
They must rely only on themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They are called prisoners of hope and promised double restoration
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:12 calls believers prisoners of hope and promises that God will render double unto them.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God' in Zechariah 9:7 imply about faithfulness?
options: Those who remain faithful belong to God and will govern
questions.correctAnswer: Those who remain faithful belong to God and will govern
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:7 states that those who remain will be for God and become governors, indicating the reward of faithfulness.

questions.question: What is the significance of God encamping about His house as described in Zechariah 9:8 for Christian living?
options: God’s protection surrounds His people against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protection surrounds His people against enemies
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:8 says God encamps about His house because of the army and oppressors, symbolizing divine protection.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 9:9 describes the King as being proud and riding a horse.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 clearly states the King is lowly and rides upon an ass and a colt, not a horse.

questions.question: True or False: Zechariah 9:11 indicates God delivers prisoners by the blood of the covenant.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:11 states that by the blood of the covenant, God has sent forth prisoners from the pit.

hard.title: Zechariah Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Zechariah Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 9:13, what has the LORD done in relation to Judah and Ephraim?
options: Bent Judah, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up Zion's sons against Greece
Destroyed Judah and Ephraim for their disobedience
Given Judah and Ephraim peace and rest
Separated Judah and Ephraim from the nations
questions.correctAnswer: Bent Judah, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up Zion's sons against Greece
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:13 explicitly states, 'When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece,' indicating God's active preparation and empowerment of Judah and Ephraim for conflict against Greece.

questions.question: In Zechariah 9:14, what imagery is used to describe the LORD's intervention?
options: His arrow going forth as lightning and blowing the trumpet with whirlwinds of the south
A lion roaring among the nations
A flood washing away the enemies
questions.correctAnswer: His arrow going forth as lightning and blowing the trumpet with whirlwinds of the south
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:14 describes the LORD’s visible presence and power using the imagery of an arrow going forth as lightning and the blowing of the trumpet accompanied by whirlwinds of the south, emphasizing swift and mighty divine action.

questions.question: What does Zechariah 9:15 say about the LORD of hosts' defense of His people?
options: They shall devour and subdue with sling stones, make noise as through wine, and be filled like bowls and altar corners
He will protect them with a shield of fire
He will send angels to fight on their behalf
He will provide them with strong walls and fortresses
questions.correctAnswer: They shall devour and subdue with sling stones, make noise as through wine, and be filled like bowls and altar corners
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:15 explains that the LORD of hosts will defend His people such that they will devour and subdue with sling stones, make noises like those made through wine, and be abundantly filled, using rich metaphorical language to convey victory and celebration.

questions.question: According to Zechariah 9:16, how will the LORD save His people?
options: As the flock of his people, making them stones of a crown, lifted as an ensign upon his land
By delivering them through a mighty flood
By sending a prophet to instruct them
By granting them peace through foreign kings
questions.correctAnswer: As the flock of his people, making them stones of a crown, lifted as an ensign upon his land
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:16 uses the typology of the flock and the stones of a crown to describe the LORD’s saving action, emphasizing both protection and exaltation of His people on His land.

questions.question: What blessings does Zechariah 9:17 associate with the LORD's goodness and beauty?
options: Corn making young men cheerful and new wine making maids glad
Gold and silver enriching the people
The sun shining forever without clouds
questions.correctAnswer: Corn making young men cheerful and new wine making maids glad
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:17 directly links the LORD’s goodness and beauty to agricultural blessings: corn and new wine, which cause joy among young men and maids, symbolizing prosperity and celebration.

questions.question: In Zechariah 9:15, what is the significance of the people making noise 'as through wine'?
options: It symbolizes joyful celebration and intoxicated victory
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes joyful celebration and intoxicated victory
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:15 uses the simile 'make a noise as through wine' to convey exuberant joy and celebration after divine victory, illustrating the emotional response of the people.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'חֶבְלִי' (chevli) in Zechariah 9:13 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Bow (as in a weapon)
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'חֶבְלִי' (chevli) in Zechariah 9:13 refers to a bow, specifically the weapon used to shoot arrows, fitting the context of 'filled the bow with Ephraim' to symbolize readiness for battle.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Zechariah 9:13 to 9:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiastic structure
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:13–16 exhibits a chiastic structure, where ideas about judgment, divine protection, and exaltation are mirrored to emphasize God's sovereign intervention, a common prophetic literary device.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the prophecy of the King coming lowly on a donkey in Zechariah 9:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 21:5
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:5 directly cites Zechariah 9:9 in the account of Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem, fulfilling the prophecy of a king coming lowly, riding on a donkey.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to Zechariah 9:10's promise of peace and dominion from sea to sea?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 72:8
questions.explanation: Psalm 72:8 speaks of a king whose dominion extends from sea to sea, paralleling Zechariah 9:10’s promise of peace and universal rule, emphasizing messianic kingship and peace.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes Zechariah 9:13 in the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Zechariah 9:12
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:12 directly precedes 9:13 and speaks to prisoners of hope, preparing the context for the divine empowerment described in 9:13.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Zechariah 9:14 where 'the LORD shall be seen over them' and 'his arrow shall go forth as the lightning'?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:14 employs metaphorical language to depict divine power and presence, using imagery of lightning and arrows to symbolize swift and powerful action by God.

questions.question: The phrase 'lifted up as an ensign upon his land' in Zechariah 9:16 is an example of what typological theme common in the Old Testament?
options: Exaltation of God's people as a banner of victory
questions.correctAnswer: Exaltation of God's people as a banner of victory
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:16 uses the typology of an ensign (banner) to symbolize the exaltation and visible prominence of God’s people, a common theme representing divine favor and victory.

questions.question: The mention of 'whirlwinds of the south' in Zechariah 9:14 reflects a cultural and historical context of which geographical region's weather phenomena?
options: Arabian desert winds from the south
questions.correctAnswer: Arabian desert winds from the south
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:14’s 'whirlwinds of the south' alludes to the hot, powerful desert winds known historically to come from the Arabian south, highlighting the sudden and fierce divine intervention.

questions.question: The statement 'corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids' in Zechariah 9:17 is an example of which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:17 uses parallelism by pairing young men with corn and maids with new wine, a common Hebrew poetic device emphasizing balance and harmony in blessings.

theological.title: Zechariah Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Zechariah Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Zechariah 9:1 teach about God's nature in relation to Israel's focus?
options: God is the ultimate object of Israel's hope and vision
God is distant and unknowable to the tribes of Israel
God delegates authority to earthly kings over Israel
God's presence is limited to the land of Hadrach
questions.correctAnswer: God is the ultimate object of Israel's hope and vision
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:1 states that 'the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the LORD,' indicating that God is the central focus and hope of Israel.

questions.question: What doctrine of divine judgment and sovereignty is taught in Zechariah 9:4 regarding Tyrus?
options: God will judge and overthrow even the mightiest human strongholds
God will protect Tyrus because of its wisdom
Tyrus will triumph over Israel by its riches
God's judgment is limited to Israel's enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God will judge and overthrow even the mightiest human strongholds
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:4 declares that the Lord will cast out Tyrus and smite her power, showing divine sovereignty over human power and wealth.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the Messianic King is taught in Zechariah 9:9?
options: The Messiah will come as a humble and just King, bringing salvation
The Messiah will come as a conquering warrior on a horse
The Messiah is an earthly king with political ambitions
The Messiah will be a priest but not a king
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah will come as a humble and just King, bringing salvation
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 describes the King coming 'lowly, and riding upon an ass,' emphasizing humility, justice, and salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Zechariah 9:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine protection
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:8 states that God will 'encamp about mine house' so that no oppressor shall pass through, indicating His protective care.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Zechariah 9:10 through the promise of peace and dominion?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:10 speaks of cutting off war implements and establishing dominion from sea to sea, demonstrating God's sovereign rule over all nations.

questions.question: How does Zechariah 9:9 prepare for the New Testament fulfillment of the Messianic entry?
options: It prophesies the humble Triumphal Entry of Jesus on a donkey
It anticipates a military conquest by David's line
It predicts a priestly anointing in the temple
It forecasts a purely spiritual kingdom with no earthly manifestation
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies the humble Triumphal Entry of Jesus on a donkey
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9's description of a King coming 'lowly, and riding upon an ass' is fulfilled in Jesus' Triumphal Entry (cf. Matthew 21:5), connecting prophecy to gospel narrative.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Zechariah 9:11 make with the theme of covenant and deliverance?
options: It connects the blood of the covenant with the release of prisoners, prefiguring Christ's saving work
It emphasizes national military victory without divine intervention
It indicates strict legalism as the path to freedom
It highlights human effort in overcoming captivity
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the blood of the covenant with the release of prisoners, prefiguring Christ's saving work
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:11 mentions 'by the blood of thy covenant' God sending forth prisoners, pointing to salvation through covenant sacrifice, analogous to Christ’s atonement.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 9:11 and Zechariah 9:12 teach about hope and restoration?
options: God’s covenantal faithfulness ensures deliverance and double restoration for the prisoners of hope
Human works are the basis for restoration
Restoration is limited to physical territory without spiritual meaning
Hope is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenantal faithfulness ensures deliverance and double restoration for the prisoners of hope
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:11–12 together declare that by covenant blood God frees prisoners and promises double restoration, emphasizing hope anchored in divine faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 9:13 and Zechariah 9:14 teach about divine empowerment in spiritual warfare?
options: God empowers His people as instruments of victory with divine intervention like lightning and trumpet
Victory is achieved solely by human military prowess
Divine power is hidden and passive in battle
Spiritual warfare is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers His people as instruments of victory with divine intervention like lightning and trumpet
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:13-14 describes God raising up sons against enemies and His arrow going forth as lightning, illustrating divine empowerment for conquest.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 9:15 and Zechariah 9:16 teach about God's salvation and the identity of His people?
options: God defends and saves His people, who become exalted like stones of a crown
Salvation is anonymous and without communal identity
God’s people are passive recipients without active defense
Salvation is limited to earthly prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God defends and saves His people, who become exalted like stones of a crown
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:15–16 depict the LORD defending and saving His people, who are then lifted up 'as the stones of a crown,' emphasizing divine salvation and exalted identity.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Zechariah 9:10 is unrealistic in promising universal peace and dominion. What does Zechariah 9:10 actually teach?
options: The Messiah will establish a reign of peace extending from sea to sea
The prophecy only applies to Israel's immediate neighbors
The passage predicts total annihilation of all nations
It emphasizes human political achievement without divine help
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah will establish a reign of peace extending from sea to sea
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:10 promises the cutting off of war and a dominion 'from sea even to sea,' teaching the Messianic reign of peace and sovereignty over all lands.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's judgment and purification is taught in Zechariah 9:7?
options: God removes abominations and purifies His people, transforming even enemies into governors for His purposes
God abandons rebellious nations without hope of restoration
God's judgment is arbitrary and unredeeming
God leaves the proud Philistines unpunished
questions.correctAnswer: God removes abominations and purifies His people, transforming even enemies into governors for His purposes
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:7 speaks of God taking away 'his abominations' and making the remnant a governor, highlighting purification and sovereign restoration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Zechariah 9:17 concerning God's provision and goodness?
questions.correctAnswer: Goodness
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:17 praises God's goodness and beauty, linking it to the joy brought by corn and new wine, highlighting divine providence and kindness.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Zechariah 9:6-7 make with God's plan for the Gentiles?
options: God will humble the Philistines and incorporate the remnant for His purposes, indicating the inclusion of Gentiles
The Gentiles are permanently excluded from God's covenant
God will destroy all Philistine descendants without exception
Gentiles are irrelevant to God's covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God will humble the Philistines and incorporate the remnant for His purposes, indicating the inclusion of Gentiles
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:6-7 shows God cutting off Philistine pride but also making survivors 'for our God' and governors, pointing to Gentile inclusion.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Zechariah 9:9 and Zechariah 9:10 teach about the nature of the Messianic kingdom?
options: The Messianic kingdom is both humble in its coming and universal in its peace and dominion
The kingdom is purely spiritual with no earthly manifestation
The kingdom depends on human military conquest alone
The kingdom excludes Gentiles and focuses only on Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Messianic kingdom is both humble in its coming and universal in its peace and dominion
questions.explanation: Zechariah 9:9 describes a humble King, while 9:10 promises His dominion from sea to sea and peace, teaching the dual nature of the kingdom.
